Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a run-of-show into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme run-of-show and deliver a live timeline: Product Launch Evening: Run of Show for 200 guests
Resource limits: one stage, one projector, crew call 17:00, doors 18:00, program over by 20:00, venue resets at 21:00.
Everything must be finished by 21:00.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Product Launch Evening: Run of Show

Venue: the main hall, 200 seats, one stage with a single projector and a two-microphone PA, and a foyer with a bar. Crew: one producer calling the show, one AV technician, two front-of-house staff and the caterers. Crew call is 5:00 pm, doors are scheduled for 6:00 pm, and the program must be over by 8:00 pm so the reception can run before the venue resets at 9:00 pm.

Pre-show
The AV technician runs a full line check of the projector, clicker and both microphones; allow 30 minutes. The producer then walks the CEO and the product lead through the stage for a 20-minute rehearsal of the keynote transitions. Meanwhile front-of-house sets up the registration desk and lays out name badges, which takes 45 minutes, then does a 15-minute walkthrough of the foyer and the seating. Catering sets the bar and the canapé stations in the foyer over 60 minutes.

Doors
Doors open on the producer's call, not before front-of-house confirms the walkthrough is done. Guests arrive and register over 30 minutes while a welcome playlist runs in the hall and the bar serves drinks. When registration closes, front-of-house ushers guests to their seats, which takes 5 minutes.

Program
The host opens the program as soon as the hall is seated and welcomes the audience for 5 minutes. The CEO keynote begins on the host's cue and runs 20 minutes; the AV technician brings up the deck. Straight after the keynote the technician plays a 2-minute product video from the booth, and the product lead follows with a 25-minute live demo. A moderated Q&A follows for about 20 minutes, no less than 15 and no more than 25; the moderator closes it when the questions run dry or the clock says so. When the moderator hands back, the host closes the program in 5 minutes and invites everyone to the reception.

Reception
The foyer bar reopens as soon as the host closes, and catering circulates canapés for 45 minutes. Front-of-house breaks down the registration desk once the last guests have left the hall, about 15 minutes, and the AV technician strikes the stage over 30 minutes after the hall is clear.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

End your reply with the same read-back as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json
{
  "summary": "one paragraph: what is being made, for how many, by when, under what constraints",
  "servesOrScale": "8 people",
  "deadline": "2026-11-26T18:00:00",
  "constraints": ["one oven", "two burners", "two cooks"]
}
```

**Read-back.** This is the run-of-show for a Product Launch Evening, a one-off live show for 200 guests in a main hall with 200 seats, staged on a single stage fed by one projector and a two-microphone PA, with a registration desk and a bar in the foyer. The people working it are a producer calling the show, one AV technician, two front-of-house staff, and the caterers (whose crew size the text never states); the guests are the audience rather than a crew. Everything is anchored to a fixed clock: crew call at 5:00 pm, doors at 6:00 pm, the program itself over by 8:00 pm so the reception can run, and the venue resetting at 9:00 pm as the hard stop by which everything must be finished. The scarcity is real and singular — one stage, one projector, one PA with exactly two microphones, one bar — so the line check, the CEO/product-lead rehearsal, the keynote deck, the product video and the Q&A all have to share the same equipment and the same room in sequence. There are genuine holds and readiness gates: doors may not open until front-of-house confirms its foyer-and-seating walkthrough; the ushers only move once registration closes; the host opens the program only when the hall is seated; the CEO keynote starts on the host's cue, with AV bringing up the deck; the 2-minute video follows the keynote immediately; and the Q&A is the one elastic block — roughly 20 minutes, floored at 15 and capped at 25, closed by the moderator when questions run dry or the clock runs out. The aftermath is gated too: the foyer bar reopens and canapés circulate the moment the host closes, front-of-house breaks the registration desk only after the last guests leave the hall, and the AV technician strikes the stage 30 minutes after the hall is clear. Running the sequence forward leaves roughly 8 minutes of headroom under the 8:00 pm program deadline (even a full 25-minute Q&A lands about 7:57 pm) and puts the reception out well before 9:00 pm, so the binding limits are the single stage/projector/PA and the doors-cannot-open-early gate rather than the clock. One caveat, not a gap I'm filling in: the text gives no calendar date and no explicit catering start or teardown end beyond the 45-minute canapé circulation, so the deadline below is a time-of-day, not a dated timestamp.

```json
{
  "summary": "A one-off Product Launch Evening run-of-show for 200 guests in a 200-seat main hall with a single stage, one projector, a two-mic PA and a foyer bar, crewed by one producer, one AV technician and two front-of-house staff plus an unspecified number of caterers, driven by one person against a live clock: crew call 5:00 pm, doors 6:00 pm (only after front-of-house confirms its foyer and seating walkthrough), program over by 8:00 pm, reception (bar plus 45 minutes of canapés) after that, and venue reset at 9:00 pm as the hard stop everything must be finished by. The scarce resources are the single stage, projector, PA and bar, so the AV line check, the CEO/product-lead rehearsal, the keynote deck, the product video and the Q&A queue behind each other; gates include doors-held-for-walkthrough, ushers-wait-for-registration-close, host-opens-only-when-seated, keynote-on-host-cue, bar-reopens-when-host-closes, FOH teardown after the last guest leaves the hall, and AV strike 30 minutes after the hall clears; the only elastic duration is the moderated Q&A (about 20 minutes, no less than 15, no more than 25). Running it forward finishes the program with roughly 8 minutes of headroom before 8:00 pm and the reception well before the 9:00 pm reset.",
```

**The model, in my words.** A **track** is one sequential line of work owned by one performer, station or role: the steps inside it run one after another and never overlap, so if two things truly happen at the same moment they must live in two different tracks — that is the only way this program expresses simultaneity. A **step** is a single piece of work with exactly one duration kind: `fixed` (`seconds`), `variable` (`minSeconds` / `maxSeconds` / `defaultSeconds`) or `indefinite` (it runs until the person on the clock ends it), and nothing else about the step decides how long it takes. A **startTrigger** is the wire that places the step on the shared clock — `programStart` at t=0, `programStartOffset` for a fixed delay, `afterStep` / `afterStepWithBuffer` when another step ends (or starts, with `event: "start"`, plus an `offsetSeconds` or `bufferSeconds`), `manual` for a tap, `onAbort` for the abort path, and `compound` to wait for all or any of several upstreams — and that wire is how a hold or a readiness gate ("doors don't open before the walkthrough is confirmed") gets enforced rather than merely described. **`stepId`s are globally unique**, not unique within a track, so a trigger can name one specific step anywhere in the program and still be unambiguous. Every **`task`** a step occupies must have a matching **`resourceConstraints`** entry, and its `maxConcurrent` is the mechanism that stops two steps from occupying the one stage, the one projector or the two-microphone PA at the same instant; the constraint is a limit the live runner enforces, not a comment. **Repetition is data, not duplication**: n trays, n samples or n aircraft become `replicates: {count: n, mode: "serial" | "parallel" | "stagger"}` on ONE step, never n copied steps or tracks; whatever follows each repetition chains with `{"type":"afterStep","stepId":"<step>","instances":"each"}`, the step that waits for every instance takes `{"instances":"all"}`, and when the holding area between them only fits k at a time (`maxInFlight: k`) the upstream step is held back instead of the downstream one being stranded — and in this run-of-show, since every step is a physically distinct piece of work by a named person, replication has nothing to bite on.

**Constraints I expect here.** I read "one stage, one projector" plus a two-microphone PA as four separate single-slot resources: `stage` (1), `projector` (1), `pa` (1 — the two mics are one PA system, not two slots; both mics are checked and used together) and `booth`/`videoPlayback` is not a scarce thing because it is the AV technician's own position, so I will not invent a limit for it. The foyer `bar` is one physical bar (1), and `registrationDesk` is one desk (1). The genuinely shared scarce items are the stage and the projector, which the line check, the rehearsal, the keynote deck, the video and the demo all contend for. **People** are the tighter limit: the producer, the AV technician and the two front-of-house staff are four distinct people, so `actors` is 4 — the caterers work the foyer bar and canapés and are not one of the four roles I am scheduling by name, and the host / CEO / product lead / moderator are on-stage roles whose time is spoken for by the program itself but who are not crew I am assigning to crew tasks.

```json
{
  "acknowledgement": "tracks are sequential lines of work and anything simultaneous needs its own track; one duration kind per step (fixed / variable / indefinite); triggers (programStart, programStartOffset, afterStep, afterStepWithBuffer, manual, onAbort, compound) wire steps to the clock or to each other; stepIds are unique across the whole program; every task a step occupies needs a matching resourceConstraints entry whose maxConcurrent is what prevents two steps sharing one stage, projector or PA; repeated work of n instances is replicates on ONE step (never n copied steps) with instances:each to chain per instance, instances:all for the barrier, and maxInFlight until when a holding area only fits k",
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "stage", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "projector", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "pa", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "bar", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "registrationDesk", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "foyer", "maxConcurrent": 2 },
    { "task": "prep", "maxConcurrent": 4 }
  ],
  "actors": 4
}
```

I kept "sets the bar and the canapé stations ... over 60 minutes" as **one** step because it is one crew, one stretch of time, one 60-minute block, and I folded the AV technician "bringing up the deck" into the keynote step because the text gives it no duration of its own (it is a cue, not a timed activity). Two entries are **instants, not durations** — `doors-open` (the producer's call) and `bar-reopen` — so they carry `fixed: 0` seconds and exist purely as milestones; if you dislike zero-length steps they collapse into the trigger of the step after them and the extraction loses nothing. I added **no** inferred steps: everything here is stated, and I would rather not invent a duration (there is no preheat/rest equivalent in this show). Durations stated with a range are `variable`; "about 15 minutes" and "45 minutes" are single figures, so they stay `fixed`.
